subject: [PATCH] mm/hugetlb: allow crashkernel to reuse hugetlb CMA memory

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the new suffix in crashkernel=size,hugetlb_cma does not provide any additional information beyond what is already stated in the documentation for crashkernel=size,cma. They suggested reusing existing hugetlb CMA memory first and reserving a dedicated area only for what hugetlb CMA does not cover.
reviews.raw_body:
The crashkernel=size,cma documentation already says that pages allocated
from the range are not in the vmcore and that it should not be used if
dumping of userspace memory is intended. HugeTLB pages are userspace
memory. I don't see what a new suffix makes explicit that ",cma" does
not already.

Why not let crashkernel=size,cma take hugetlb CMA first and reserve a
dedicated area only for what hugetlb CMA does not cover? With
hugetlb_cma=6G crashkernel=2G,cma there would be no extra CMA at all.
With hugetlb_cma=2G crashkernel=4G,cma the crash kernel would reuse the
2G and a dedicated 2G area would be reserved for the rest. Either way,
nobody has to learn a new option.

The catch is ordering. reserve_crashkernel_cma() runs from setup_arch(),
but hugetlb_cma_reserve() runs later, from mm_core_init_early(). The arch
code could record the size and leave the reservation to generic code
right after hugetlb_cma_reserve(). That is still memblock time, so the
remainder can be declared there. An early_initcall is too late for that.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a need for revision and agreed to restructure the patch in version 2 (v2) to address Kiryl's feedback.
reviews.raw_body:
Makes sense to me, I will rewrite it in the above way and send v2.

Thanks for the review!
Usama

2026-11-04.patch_summary: This patch allows the crashkernel to reuse existing hugetlb CMA memory, enabling systems that already reserve large amounts of memory with hugetlb_cma= to use some of it for the capture kernel's working set after a crash. The patch introduces a new suffix 'hugetlb_cma' for the crashkernel parameter, which allows specifying an additional amount of memory to be reused from existing HugeTLB allocations. This approach ensures that the running kernel can still access the full 6G of hugetlb CMA memory during normal operation, while providing the capture kernel with additional working memory after a crash.
